questions.question: Which of these MFIs are NOT regulated by the RBI?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Non-profit MFIs.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Non-profit MFIs are **not** regulated by the RBI.
 
• **Small Finance Bank-led MFI**s are regulated by the RBI as they are categorized as banks.
 
• **Bank-led MFIs **are also regulated by the RBI as they are subsidiaries of banks.
 
• **NBFC MFIs** are regulated by the RBI as they are categorized as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs).
 
• Non-profit MFIs are typically registered as** societies or trusts **and operate on a not-for-profit basis.
 
• They are **not required** to be registered with the RBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **RBI** (Reserve Bank of India) is the **central bank of the country** and is responsible for **regulating and supervising** the financial sector.
 
• **Small Finance Banks** are a new category of banks in India that provide **financial services to the unbanked and underbanked **sections of the society.
 
• **Bank-led MFI**s are **microfinance institutions** that are owned by banks.
 
• **NBFC MFIs **are microfinance institutions that are registered as Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) and provide **microcredit **to the underserved and unbanked segments of the society.

questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj is associated with which form of dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj** is associated with the classical Indian dance form of **Kathak.**
 
• He is a renowned Kathak **dancer, choreographer, and instructor** from India.
 
• Kathak is a **North Indian classical dance** form that involves intricate footwork, pirouettes, and facial expressions to depict various emotions and stories.
 
• Pandit Birju Maharaj is the torchbearer of the **Lucknow gharana of Kathak** and has been honored with several prestigious awards for his contribution to Indian classical dance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chhau** is a semi-classical dance form from **eastern India.**

 
 
• It involves **acrobatics and martial arts.**
 
 
 
• **Kuchipudi **is a classical dance form from the state of** Andhra Pradesh.**
 
 
• It involves** storytelling **and intricate footwork.
 
 
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance form from the southern state of** Kerala.**
 
 
• It involves elaborate makeup, costumes, and facial expressions to **depict mythological stories.**

questions.question: Which cell organelles are known as the cell's post office?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Golgi apparatus.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Golgi apparatus** is known as the** cell's post office** because it packages and distributes** molecules** (proteins and lipids) to different parts of the cell and outside the cell.
 
• It **modifies, sorts, and packages** the molecules in **vesicles** and sends them to their intended destinations.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is composed of stacks of flattened membranous sacs called** cisternae,** which are responsible for carrying out the aforementioned functions.
 
• The Golgi apparatus is present in **eukaryotic cells**, which include animal and plant cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The nucleus** is known as the control center of the cell, as it contains** genetic material (DNA).**

 
 
• It is responsible for regulating **cell growth, division, and metabolism.**
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes **are responsible for synthesizing proteins in the cell,
 
 
• They are either free in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **endoplasmic reticulum.**
 
 
 
• **Plastids** are organelles found only in** plant cells** and are responsible for functions such as** photosynthesis, storage, and pigment synthesis**.
 
 
• Plastids include** chloroplasts, chromoplasts, and leucoplasts.**

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: which element of group 13 has the atomic number 113 and its electronic configuration is [Rn] 5f¹⁴6d¹⁰7s²7p¹?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nihonium.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The element with atomic number **113** belongs to group 13 of the periodic table, which is also known as the** boron group.**
 
• The electronic configuration **[Rn] 5f¹⁴6d¹⁰7s²7p¹ **belongs to the element **Nihonium,** which was officially named in **2016 **and is a synthetic element that is not found naturally on Earth.
 
• Nihonium is a **highly unstable **and **radioactive element**, with a very short half-life of only a few seconds, and its properties are still being studied by scientists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Group 13** elements are characterized by having **three valence electrons** in their outermost shell, which makes them** reactive **and able to form compounds with other elements.
 
• **Gallium** is a **soft, silvery metal** that has a **low melting point** and is used in a variety of applications, such as in **semiconductors, LEDs, and alloys.**
 
• **Indium** is a **rare, silvery-white metal **that is used in electronics, as well as in **coatings, alloys, **and other industrial applications.
 
• **Thallium** is a** toxic, bluish-white metal **that is used in electronics, as well as in **pesticides, rodenticides**, and other chemicals.
 
• It is also a **radioactive isotope** that is used in medical imaging.
 
• Thallium is also a** group 13 element**, but it has a higher atomic number than Nihonium and a different electronic configuration.

• **Mining **is a relatively small sector in India and employs a** small percentage **of the workforce.

questions.question: Structural composition of the economy refers to:

options.text: contribution of various sectors to the GDP
rural and urban distribution of the population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**contribution of various sectors to the GDP.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Structural composition of the economy** refers to the contribution of various sectors to the **GDP. **
 
• It is a measure of the **percentage of economic activity **that each sector contributes to the overall GDP of a country.
 
• The sectors typically include **agriculture, manufacturing, services, and others.**
 
• The structural composition of the economy can vary significantly between countries and can be an indicator of the** level of development.**
 
• Changes in the structural composition of the economy can have significant impacts on** employment, income, and economic growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Male-female distribution** of the population refers to the proportion of males and females in a population.
 
• **Private and public sector classification** refers to the types of organizations that operate in the economy, with private sector organizations being owned and operated by** individuals or groups**, and public sector organizations being owned and operated by the** government.**
 
• **Rural and urban distribution of the population** refers to the proportion of the population that lives in **rural versus urban areas**.

questions.question: The rulers of which of the following Rajput dynasties patronised Jainism and one of them is reported to have accepted Jainism under the influence of a Jain scholar Hemachandra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chalukya.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chalukya dynasty** ruled over parts of present-day **Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh **from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• The Chalukya rulers were known for their patronage of **Jainism**, as well as** Hinduism and Buddhism**.
 
• Some of the notable Jain scholars who flourished under their patronage were **Akalanka, Siddharshi, and Hemachandra.**
 
• Hemachandra was a renowned **Jain monk, poet, and scholar** who lived during the 12th century CE.
 
• He is said to have converted the Chalukya king **Kumarapala to Jainism **and wrote several works on** Jain philosophy, grammar, and literature.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pratihara dynasty**:

 
 
• This Rajput dynasty ruled over parts of present-day **northern and central India **from the 6th to the 11th century CE.
 
• While they were known for their **military prowess **and **patronage of the arts**, there is no record of their significant association with Jainism.
 
 
 
• **Parmar dynasty**:
 
 
• This was another Rajput dynasty that ruled over parts of present-day **Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan** from the 9th to the 14th century CE.
 
• They were known for their patronage of** Hinduism and Jainism**, as well as their architectural achievements such as the famous Khajuraho temples.
 
 
 
• **Chahman dynasty**:
 
 
• This Rajput dynasty ruled over parts of present-day **Rajasthan and Gujarat **from the 6th to the 12th century CE.
 
• They were known for their **patronage of Jainism,** as well as their military exploits and architectural achievements such as the **fort of Taragarh**.

questions.question: Since 2004, which of the following states in India is the permanent venue of the International Film Festival of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goa.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goa** has been the permanent venue for **IFFI** since** 2004.**
 
• **International Film Festival of India **(IFFI) is an annual film festival organized by the** Ministry of Information and Broadcasting,** Government of India.
 
• The festival was started in **1952** and has been held in different cities across India.
 
• The festival showcases a wide **range of films** from across the world, including feature films, documentaries, and short films.
 
• The festival also includes **panel discussions, workshops, and masterclasses **with industry experts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Under the support of India's first prime minister, the** Films Division** of the Government of India hosted the inaugural edition of IFFI.
 
• The Festival was first held in Mumbai from **January 24 to February 1, 1952,** and it thereafter traveled to **Madras, Delhi, Calcutta, and Trivandrum.**
 
• The** 35th edition **of the International Film Festival of India marked the festival's transition to a permanent location in** Goa** and global competition beginning in **2004.**
 
• Every year, it takes place in the months of **November and December. **

questions.question: Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for founding the Grameen Bank and pioneering the concepts of microcredit and microfinance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Yunus.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Yunus** is a prominent member of **civil society, banker, economist**, and **social entrepreneur **from Bangladesh.
 
• In recognition of his creating the** Grameen Bank** and developing the ideas of** microcredit and microfinance,** he was granted the **Nobel Peace Prize** in **2006.**
 
• Entrepreneurs who are too impoverished to be eligible for** conventional bank loans **are granted these loans. 
 
• Together, Yunus and Grameen Bank received the **Nobel Peace Priz**e "for their efforts to create economic and social development from below through microcredit."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grameen Bank** is a **microfinance organization** that provides small loans to impoverished individuals who **lack collateral** or **credit history.**
 
• **Microcredit **refers to the provision of small loans to** low-income individuals** or groups who are unable to access traditional banking services.
 
• **Microfinance** is a broader term that encompasses a range of financial services, including **microcredit, savings, insurance, and remittances**, that are provided to low-income individuals or groups.

questions.question: Exports of mangoes by India are a part of _______ method of measurement of its national income.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**expenditure.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Exports of mangoes** by India contribute to the **expenditure method** of measuring its national income because it represents a portion of the country's** total exports, **which is a component of its overall expenditure.
 
• The expenditure method of measuring national income is one of** three primary methods **used, along with the income method and the value-added method.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **income method **measures national income by** adding up all of the income** earned by individuals and businesses in a country, while the value-added method calculates national income by **subtracting the cost of inputs** from the revenue generated by businesses.
 
• Circular income refers to the** flow of money b**etween different sectors of an economy.
 
• **Value-added** measures the increase in **value of a product **at each stage of production, rather than simply the final sale price.

questions.question: Which is the biggest tributary of the upper Brahmaputra that originates in the Tibetan Himalayas and winds its way into India through Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subansiri.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Subansiri **is the biggest tributary of the **upper Brahmaputra.**
 
• It originates in the** Tibetan Himalayas** and flows through **Arunachal Pradesh** before joining the **Brahmaputra in Assam.**
 
• The Brahmaputra River is one of the major rivers in Asia, flowing through **China, India, and Bangladesh.**
 
• It is also known as the **Tsangpo-Brahmaputra River** system.
 
• Some of the other tributaries of the Brahmaputra include the** Lohit, Dibang, and Kameng rivers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A tributary of the** Krishna River **is the** Yerala River.**

 
 
• It comes from the far north of **Khatav taluka in Satara district,** near the Mhaskoba highlands.
 
 
 
• The **Musi River** flows through **Telangana, India**, and is a significant tributary of the Krishna River in the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
• **Hyderabad** is located along the Musi River's banks.
 
 
 
• One of the rivers that flows through the T**apti River Basin** is the **Aner River.**
 
 
• It is situated in the Indian state of **Maharashtra**, close to Hisale.
 
 
 
• The Brahmaputra river basin is home to a diverse range of **flora and fauna**, including the endangered Gangetic dolphin and the one-horned rhinoceros.
 
• The Brahmaputra River is an important source of water for** irrigation, fishing, transportation, and hydropower generation** in the northeastern region of India.

questions.question: Which colour of light from VIBGYOR has minimum energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Red.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The energy of light is** inversely proportional** to its wavelength.
 
• Therefore, the light with the **longest wavelength,** i.e. **red**, has the **least energy.**
 
• The colours of VIBGYOR are arranged in **increasing order** of their** wavelengths.**
 
• Hence, **violet** has the** highest energy **and red has the least.
 
• **Green** is the colour of light with a wavelength between yellow and blue.
 
• It has **more energy** than yellow but less than blue.
 
• **Yellow** is the colour of light with a wavelength between green and orange.
 
• It has** less energy** than green but more than orange.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **VIBGYOR** stands for** Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red.**

 
 
• These are the** seven colours **of the visible spectrum of light.
 
 
 
• Violet has the **shortest wavelength** and the highest energy among the colours of VIBGYOR.
 
• **Indigo** is a colour that lies between **blue and violet **in the spectrum.
 
 
• It is not always distinguishable from blue and is **not** considered a separate colour by some people.
 
 
 
• **Orange** is a colour that lies between **yellow and red** in the spectrum.
 
 
• It has **more energy** than red but less than yellow.

questions.question: Tulip Festival is famous in which city?

questions.question: In August 2021, Ram Nath Kovind granted assent to which Constitution Amendment Act empowering states and UTs to identify and specify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**105th.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The One Hundred and Fifth Amendment (or 105th Constitutional Amendment) to the Constitution of India- officially known as The Constitution (One Hundred and Fifth Amendment) Act, 2021- restored the power of State governments to recognise socially and educationally backward classes (SEBCs).<

questions.question: In which of the following economic accounts are transfer payments included?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Government account.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Transfer payments** are included in the **government account** of economic accounts.
 
• Transfer payments are payments made by the government to** individuals or businesses **without any expectation of goods or services in return.
 
• Examples of transfer payments include **social security, welfare, and unemployment** benefits.
 
• The inclusion of transfer payments in the government account helps in measuring the government's role in **income redistribution **and social welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **household account **refers to the **income and expenditure** of households.

 
 
• **Parents and kids** who live with you are considered immediate family members and can use the account.
 
 
 
• The **appropriation account **refers to the **allocation and utilization of funds** by the government for specific purposes such as infrastructure development or defense spending.
 
 
• An appropriation account for a business indicates how** profits are allocated** and held.
 
• It displays the way in which **profits are split **up among partners in a partnership.
 
 
 
• The **production account **refers to the value of goods and services produced by different sectors of the economy.
 
 
• It is designed for both **industry and institutional** sectors.
 
 
 
• **Transfer payments **are an important tool for governments to address** income inequality** and provide a safety net for vulnerable sections of society.

questions.question: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, now known as Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, was first enacted in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2005.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act** was first enacted in the year **2005.**
 
• The Act is a **social security scheme **that provides a legal guarantee for **100 days of employment** in a financial year to adult members of rural households who are willing to do unskilled manual work.
 
• The Act aims to address the issues of** poverty and unemployment** in rural India by providing a source of livelihood to the rural poor and strengthening the rural economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A** third of the employment** made available under the MGNREGA are guaranteed to** women.**
 
• It is worth noting that the idea of a **rural employment **guarantee was first proposed in the **1990s** by the National Commission on Rural Labour, which recommended a minimum of **100 days of employment** for rural households.
 
• It is worth noting that the Act has undergone several amendments since its enactment in** 2005,** including the inclusion of women as a separate category of workers in** 2008 **and the introduction of a provision for unemployment allowance in** 2013.**

questions.question: The celebration of Christmas, Eid, and Holi in school is an example of making children learn fundamental duties as well. Which of the following fundamental duties advocates about this type of ideals?

options.text: To defend the country and render national service
To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To promote harmony and spirit of common brotherhood.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Celebrating festivals **of different religions in school promotes the idea of** unity in diversity,** which is the essence of promoting **harmony and common brotherhood.**
 
• By participating in these celebrations, children learn to respect and appreciate different cultures and religions, which is important for building a **cohesive society.**
 
• This fundamental duty also promotes the idea of** secularism,** which is a key feature of our constitution.
 
• By learning about different festivals, children also learn about the** history and traditions** associated with them, which is a form of cultural education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "To defend the country and render national service," is related to the duty of citizens to protect the **sovereignty, integrity, and security** of the country.

 
 
• This includes serving in the armed forces, volunteering for national service, and being prepared to** defend** the country in times of crisis.
 
 
 
• "To develop the scientific temper," is about the duty of citizens to have a** rational and scientific outlook **towards life.
 
 
• This includes promoting** scientific research**, fostering a** spirit of inquiry,** and rejecting superstitions and blind faith.
 
 
 
• "To safeguard public property and to abjure violence," is about the duty of citizens to** respect public property **and to refrain from using violence as a means of achieving their goals.
 
 
• This includes protecting public property from **damage or destruction,** and resolving conflicts through peaceful means.

questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** in India is a large region of elevated land that lies to the south of the** Indo-Gangetic Plain.**
 
• It is mainly composed of **Precambrian rocks** that are millions of years old.
 
• The plateau covers parts of several Indian states, including **Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Kerala.**
 
• However, **Punjab** is **not **a part of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• It is located in the northwest of India and is mainly composed of **alluvial plains and river valleys.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Peninsular Plateau** is characterized by its composition of ancient** crystalline, igneous, and metamorphic** rocks.
 
• **Maharashtra** is a part of the Peninsular Plateau and includes the Deccan Plateau, which is a** large volcanic plateau** that covers much of central and southern India.
 
• **Madhya Pradesh **is also a part of the Peninsular Plateau and includes the **Vindhya and Satpura **mountain ranges, as well as parts of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• **Tamil Nadu** is a state in the south of India that is also a part of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• It includes the **Eastern Ghats mountain range** and the **Nilgiri Hills.**

questions.question:
Poshan Abhiyaan is a program to achieve nutritional status of children from 0 to 6 years.

Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for raising the nutrition level?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 47.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 47** states that "the State shall regard the raising of the **level of nutrition** and the **standard of living **of its people and the improvement of **public health **as among its primary duties".
 
• This article emphasizes the importance of improving the** overall health and well-being** of the citizens of India, including their nutritional status.
 
• **Poshan Abhiyaan** is a flagship scheme of the Government of India launched in** 2018 **to improve the** nutritional status** of children and pregnant women.
 
• The scheme aims to reduce** stunting, undernutrition, and low birth weight** by 2% annually and focuses on the first **1,000 day**s of a child's life.
 
• The scheme covers various interventions such as the promotion of **breastfeeding, complementary feeding, micro-nutrient supplementation, and hygiene and sanitation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 44** pertains to the **Uniform Civil Code **and aims to promote the welfare of the people by securing a uniform civil code throughout the country.
 
• **Article 46 **provides for the promotion of educational and economic interests of the** weaker sections of society,** including Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
 
• **Article 45** provides for free and compulsory education for all children until they complete the age of **14 years.**

questions.question: Who among the following is the first Indian female football player to play in the Union of European Football Association (UEFA) Women's Champions League?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manisha Kalyan.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manisha Kalyan** is the** first Indian female football** player to play in the **Union of European Football Association **(UEFA) women's Champions League.
 
• She played for **Gokulam Kerala FC** in the **2018-19 **season.
 
• Manisha Kalyan is a forward player and has represented India in various** international tournaments.**
 
• She has also played for the Indian Women's League teams like **Rising Student Club** and **Sethu FC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shanti Mallick** is a former Indian** women's football team** captain who represented India in the 1980s and early 1990s.

 
 
• She was one of the pioneers of women's football in India and played for teams like **Orissa and Bengal.**
 
 
 
• **Bala Devi** is a current Indian women's football team captain who has won many awards and accolades in her career.
 
 
• She has played for teams like** Manipur Police Sports Club** and** Rangers Women's FC** in **Scotland.**
 
 
 
• **Oinam Bembem Devi **is a former Indian women's football team captain who has represented India in various international tournaments.
 
 
• She has played for teams like** Eastern Sporting Union** and **Sethu FC **in the Indian Women's League.

questions.question: Ustad Asad Ali Khan played which of the following instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rudra Veena.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ustad Asad Ali Khan** played the **Rudra Veena**, which is a **stringed instrument** used in Indian classical music.
 
• The Rudra Veena is known for its** deep, resonant sound **and is considered one of the oldest instruments in India.
 
• The **Hindu **referred to Khan, who played in the **dhrupad style,** as the greatest rudra veena player alive in India.
 
• In **2008,** he received the Indian civilian distinction of **Padma Bhushan.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Rudra Veena** is often played by dhrupad musicians, who are known for their **slow and meditative style** of singing.
 
• The** Algoza** is typically played by two musicians simultaneously, with one playing the** melody **and the other playing the drone.
 
• **Algoza **is a **double flute** used in Punjabi folk music, while the** Sitar** is a **plucked string** instrument commonly used in Indian classical music.
 
• The Sitar is known for its d**istinctive sound** and is often used in film music as well as classical performances.
 
• **Ravanahatha **is traditionally played by a community of musicians known as** Bhopas**, who use the instrument to accompany their **epic storytelling** performances.
 
• Ravanahatha is a bowed string instrument used in** Rajasthan, India, **and is believed to be one of the oldest stringed instruments in the world.
